title: Probe-Free Session-Hijacking Detection in AI-Native 6G Edge Networks Using Digital-Twin-Guided Service Decisions
content: Programmable edge networks, and the AI-native control envisioned for 6G, make frequent control decisions while keeping predictive models of connected devices. A reusable session credential can then let a substitute endpoint continue a legitimately authenticated session. Sender-constrained tokens mitigate this risk where they are deployed, but constrained or legacy devices, extracted keys and relay arrangements leave a residual gap that statistical continuity checking can help to close. We propose PF-TRACE (Probe-Free Twin-guided Randomized Action Control for Endpoint verification), a probe-free policy that turns decisions the network must make anyway into security evidence. Among near-equivalent edge-computing actions, the controller picks the one whose response best separates an enrolled device twin from likely impostors. We evaluated PF-TRACE using ns-3/5G-LENA 5G NR radio traces and split-inference measurements collected from Raspberry Pi and laptop hardware. These measurements were replayed in a Python-based simulator. With the false-alarm rate set to one per 10,000 genuine epochs, PF-TRACE detected about 72% of relay attacks and 56% of same-model substitutions within 500 epochs. Passive twin checking achieved 58% and 40%, respectively. Active probing at a similar cost detected 68% and 47%. Paired tests over 30 independent runs showed that the gains over passive checking were statistically significant for both attacks (p < 0.001). PF-TRACE added about 2% to p95 completion time. PF-TRACE-D, a deterministic maximum-information variant of our scheme, detected faster against non-adaptive attackers, but against a policy-aware attacker that learned the controller’s action choices its relay detection fell to 52%, whereas PF-TRACE retained 64%. Detection depends on observable response differences, so the gains narrow under heavy load and do not extend to a faster attacker that adds delay to reproduce the genuine response.
